title: How many lines and angles can four points make?
description: Four points, with no three on one line, are labelled A, B, C and D. A line is drawn through each pair of points, and then the angles at each point are named by taking the other three points two at a time.
teaching_notes: One idea: each pair of points gives one line, and at each point the other three points taken two at a time give three angles. Watch for students who count BA and AB as two lines, or who miss the angle that uses the two farthest points.

source: Now mark any four points on your paper so that no three of them are on one line. Label them A, B, C, D. Draw all possible lines going through pairs of these points. How many lines do you get? Name them. How many angles can you name using A, B, C, D? Write them all down, and mark each of them with a curve as in Fig. 2.9.
video_script.why: The child joins each pair of four points to get the lines, and at each point names the angles made by taking the other three points two at a time.
video_script.substitution: Draw a line through each pair of the points, and at each point take the other three points two at a time to name the angles.
video_script.anchor: a page with four points A, B, C and D, where no three are on one line
video_script.payoff_line: There are six lines and twelve angles

final_answer.value: There are 6 lines, AB, BC, CD, DA, AC and BD, and 12 angles, angle BAC, CAD, BAD, ADB, BDC, ADC, DCA, ACB, DCB, CBD, DBA and CBA
final_answer.spoken: there are six lines and twelve angles. The lines are eigh B, B C, C D, D eigh, eigh C and B D. The angles are three at each of the four points

never_show: the count of the lines or of the angles, before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line is drawn through each pair of the four points: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD and CD, which makes 6 lines.
No three points are on one line, so every pair gives its own line, and BA is the same line as AB.
At A the other points B, C and D, taken two at a time, give the angles BAC, CAD and BAD.
At each of the four points there are 3 angles in the same way, so there are 4 times 3, which is 12 angles.
The vertex is the middle letter in the name of each angle.
video_script.design: One idea: six pairs give six lines, and each of the four points is the vertex of three angles. The four points stay on the board, the lines are drawn one at a time, and the angles are named point by point. The method is the same way as the examples in the book on the arms and the vertex of an angle.
